**About the Role**
  
  
We are looking for an L5 Program Manager to join Delivery Product Insights & Rollouts and own product and rollout readiness across a major Uber Delivery Persona. This role sits at the intersection of Product, Tech, CX, Operations and Data, and is accountable for turning complex launch information into a clear, trusted readiness view and recommendation.
  
  
The role will likely own a Persona lane and may flex across Personas as business priorities evolve. As the broader xLOB operating model develops, the role may also contribute to Quality and continuous experience improvement.
  
  
This role requires end-to-end ownership. The right person can understand the product and technical system deeply enough to identify what can impact the customer or support experience, evaluate the evidence, challenge assumptions, drive cross-functional decisions, and hold the organization to a clear readiness bar.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Own end-to-end readiness for material product and technology rollouts within an assigned Persona, from early planning through launch, scale and post-launch monitoring
* Build and communicate a clear, decision-ready readiness POV that brings together the recommendation, evidence and break-glass metrics, risks, gaps that could change the decision, and owners / next steps

* + Partner with central capabilities to apply common standards while preserving the Persona context required for strong readiness and experience decisions.

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Missile Warning & Tracking
jobs.description:
**About the role**
------------------

Muon Space seeks a Senior Program Manager to lead delivery of next-generation satellites for national security missions, including missile warning and tracking. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of payload engineering and rapid-cycle space vehicle development.

The Senior PM is the accountable owner for delivering the program on cost, schedule, and technical performance. You will manage a multi-disciplinary internal team, subcontractors, and a critical-path vendor base for EO/IR payloads, algorithm development, avionics, and space vehicle builds. The role spans the full program lifecycle: design reviews, hardware build, integration and environmental test, launch, and on-orbit operations.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* **Program Execution**
  + Own the integrated master schedule, cost baseline, and risk register
  + Drive the program through preliminary and critical design reviews, payload and spacecraft integration, environmental test, launch, and on-orbit demonstration, meeting customer milestones and contract deliverables
  + Manage scope, cost, and period of performance against contract milestones and payment events
  + Lead day-to-day execution of the program team to the contract, running the weekly program cadence, internal design reviews, and readiness reviews; provide status and briefing content to the Mission Manager, who is the customer interface
  + Own the preparation and quality of contract deliverables, including status reports, design review packages, technical and cost data, test plans, and final reports, for delivery to the customer
  + Partner with the Mission Manager and Muon's Capture and Business Development teams on follow-on strategy
* **Subcontractor and Vendor Management**
  + Manage program subcontracts, including mission data processing and algorithm development
  + Coordinate critical-path vendors for detectors, focal plane arrays, cooler assemblies, and optics across long-lead procurements
  + Keep subcontract scope, cost, and schedule aligned with prime contract commitments
* **Technical Leadership and Risk Management**
  + Partner closely with the lead systems engineer and technical leads (payload design, AI&T, optics, electronics, software, mechanisms, thermal, mission systems) to drive technical decisions
  + Own and actively work the program risk register, including supply chain, integration, launch, and demonstration risks
  + Resolve cross-functional issues quickly and escalate to functional and program leadership when needed
* **Compliance and Reporting**
  + Ensure program execution complies with contract requirements, including U.S.-only performance, ITAR/EAR export controls, technical data rights, security requirements, and CUI handling
  + Coordinate with Contracts and Finance on subcontract changes, invoicing, and program financial reporting

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* 8+ years of professional experience in program or technical management of complex technical system development, deployment, and operations
* 5+ years of hands-on technical experience, preferably in an engineering or similar capacity, or direct ownership of a hardware development effort through design reviews to a tested product
* Direct experience with space, defense, or aerospace program planning and execution
* Demonstrated experience managing programs with multiple subcontractors and a complex critical-path supply chain
* Experience executing rapid-acquisition or prototype agreements for government customers, with familiarity navigating the government program lifecycle, technical data rights, and contract deliverables
* Active Secret U.S. security clearance
* U.S. citizenship required (Clearance required and program is ITAR-restricted)
* Excellent written communication skills; you will author or approve the program's contract deliverables

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Active Top Secret or TS/SCI clearance
* Prior experience on a missile warning, missile tracking, missile defense, or similar space-based infrared program
* Working knowledge of EO/IR sensor architectures, focal plane arrays, and cryocooler integration
* Working knowledge of missile warning data products and techniques for detection and tracking
* Experience managing programs through environmental test campaigns (TVAC, vibration, EMI/EMC)
* Experience with launch integration and early on-orbit operations

**Salary**
----------

The salary range for this role is $206,000 - $232,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

**About Muon Space**
--------------------

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

At Google, we "Focus on the user and all else will follow." UX Programs & Operations drives projects by increasing communication, streamlining the UX design process, and fostering a culture of user-centered development. You will join our multi-disciplinary UX team, collaborating with Engineering and Product Management, to create industry-leading products based on user insights.

jobs.title: Buchanan Y - ASP Program Leader (Part-time and Full-time)
jobs.description:
**Careers by** **E****mpowering Futures, Building Communities**

Imagine going to work each day knowing that your efforts positively impact individuals and communities. As a global movement and the nation's leading nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening communities through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility, the YMCA of Greater San Francisco offers more than just a job—we offer a career with a future and the opportunity to make a lasting difference in your community. At the Y, you can uncover your passion and build a lifelong career addressing some of the nation's most pressing social issues.

**Our Organizational Culture**

At the YMCA of Greater San Francisco, we are committed to demonstrating values that aim to building strong communities where you can **Be**, **Belong** and **Become.** With **Truth & Courage**, we strive to understand and act on individual and societal truths. We ensure a safe and inclusive environment with **Authenticity & Accessibility**, allowing everyone to participate according to their needs. Our approach is **Dependable & Creative**, as we respond to community needs through strong partnerships. Above all, we embody **Dignity & Empathy**, treating everyone with respect and compassion, and recognizing the inherent dignity in all individuals.

**Qualifications**  

* 18+ for elementary programs; 21+ for middle school programs.
* Associate’s degree or higher, or High School diploma/equivalent with one of the following:

o 48+ completed college units (verified by transcript),  
o Passing score on the CA Basic Education Skills Test (CBEST), or  
o Passing score on a District Instructional Aide Exam.  

* Strong teamwork and communication skills.
* Knowledge of youth development principles.
* Available Monday–Friday during program hours
* TB Test clearance within last 2 years (required for programs on school district sites).

**Preferred Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s degree in child development or related field OR equivalent professional and community experience.
* Experience working with elementary or middle school-aged youth.
* Bilingual skills in Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, or other languages.
* Knowledge of arts, dance, drama, sports, or other enrichment areas.

**Position Summary**

The After School Program Leader provides meaningful opportunities for youth in YMCA programs at local elementary and middle schools. They work under the supervision of Program Site Coordinators and Directors and are expected to demonstrate flexibility, initiative, and punctuality, with a commitment to the school-year schedule.

  

**Part-Time and Full-Time opportunities are available for After School Program Dates**:

* San Francisco Sites: August 10, 2026 – June 2, 2027
* Marin Sites: August 17, 2026 – June 11, 2027

**Job Responsibilities**

  

**Curriculum Development & Program Delivery**

* Design and implement engaging, inclusive, and theme-based curricula that reflect the developmental stages and cultural backgrounds of youth.
* Facilitate academic enrichment, tutoring, and structured outdoor recreational activities.
* Partner with staff, caregivers, and participants to plan and enhance program offerings.  
  **Supervision & Safety**
* Supervise groups of up to 20 students, ensuring a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment in alignment with YMCA and child safety protocols.
* Actively monitor participants, respond promptly to incidents, and consistently apply safety guideline  
  **Record-Keeping & Compliance**
* Maintain accurate and up-to-date program records, including attendance, emergency information, and safety documentation  
  **Communication & Engagement**
* Communicate clearly and respectfully with participants, caregivers, staff, and volunteers to support a positive program experience.  
  **Training & Development**
* Complete required safety and program training before the first shift and attend all mandatory meetings and training sessions.

**Work Environment & Physical Demands**

The After School Program Leader works in a dynamic environment at local elementary or middle school sites, including indoor classrooms and outdoor schoolyards. The role involves frequent standing, walking, and active participation in physical activities such as recreational sports and games. The environment can be fast-paced and loud, and the role may require occasional lifting of up to 20 pounds.

  

**Disclaimers**

* Must successfully complete a background screening, including criminal and employment verification. Some positions may also require a credit check.

* All duties and responsibilities are essential job functions subject to reasonable accommodation. The YMCA of Greater San Francisco promotes an equal employment opportunity workplace, which includes reasonable accommodation for otherwise qualified disabled applicants and employees. Please contact your manager if you have any questions about this policy or these job duties.

* This job description may not be all-inclusive, and employees are expected to perform other duties as assigned by management. Job descriptions and duties may be modified by management as needed.

* Job offers are conditional and contingent upon background clearance. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance and CA Fair Chance Act, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

  

**Salary Description**

The After School Program Leader position offers a compensation range of $24.00 – $25.50 per hour. This rate is based on salary benchmarking for similar roles and is aligned with grant fund approvals and requirements for the position.

It's why we provide our caregivers with continuing education and state-of-the-art facilities, like the newly remodeled Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford. This paragraph summarizes the general nature, level and purpose of the job.

Reporting to the Manager- Authorization, the Supervisor of Patient Admitting Services in Main Admitting is directly responsible for supervising the staff of the Patient Admitting Department, researching and resolving operational issues related to hospital admitting functions and for recommending policy and/or procedural changes in order to streamline the admitting practices within PAS. jobs.title: Senior Quality Manager
jobs.description:
**About Amprius**

Amprius Technologies (NYSE: AMPX) is a leader in high-energy, high-power lithium-ion batteries built on silicon anode technology. Our SiCore® and SiMaxx™ cells power unmanned aerial systems, aviation and other applications where weight and energy density matter most. Headquartered in Fremont, California, Amprius designs cells in house and produces them through a global network of contract manufacturing partners.

**The role**

We are looking for a Senior Quality Manager to own quality across Amprius, from incoming materials and contract manufacturers to the cells we ship to customers. You will lead our quality management system, earn and maintain AS9100 certification, and build a supplier and CM quality program that grows with our manufacturing network. Reporting to Managing Director, Operations. Travel up to 20%, including supplier and CM sites in Asia.

**What you will do**

**Quality management system**

* Own the QMS and lead Amprius through AS9100 certification, then maintain it through surveillance audits.
* Set quality policy, objectives and metrics, and report quality performance to leadership.
* Own document control and records requirements, in partnership with the PLM and change control rollout.

**Supplier and CM quality**

* Build the supplier quality program: audits, qualification, PPAP or first-article approval and ongoing monitoring.
* Publish quarterly scorecards (yield, cost, on-time delivery) for every active supplier and CM.
* Drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to fast closure and prevent repeat issues.
* Support new CM and second-source qualifications with Supply Chain.

**Cell quality and certification**

* Make sure every shipping product is tested and certified before shipment (UN 38.3, IEC 62133 and customer requirements).
* Lead incoming, in-process and outgoing inspection and test strategy at Fremont and at CMs.
* Lead customer quality: complaints, returns, failure analysis and 8D reports.

Continuous improvement and team

* Run Lean and Six Sigma improvement projects with measurable savings.
* Hire and develop the quality team, including supplier quality engineers assigned to specific CMs and material families.

 **Requirements**

**What you bring**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, materials science or a related technical field.
* 10+ years in quality for manufactured hardware, including 4+ years managing quality teams.
* Has led an organization through AS9100 or ISO 9001 certification as the QMS owner.
* Strong supplier quality background: audits, PPAP or FAI, and CAPA and 8D methods.
* Skilled with core quality tools: FMEA, control plans, SPC and MSA.

**Nice to have**

* Lithium-ion cell or battery quality, including UN 38.3 and IEC 62133 testing.
* Quality oversight of contract manufacturers, especially in Asia.
* ASQ CQE or CQM certification; Six Sigma Black Belt; AS9100 lead auditor.

 **Benefits**  

* Comprehensive compensation package includes base salary. Salary range for this role is X to X. Base salary will be determined based on knowledge, experience, and education.
* Health benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage. Medical options of HMO and PPO plans.
* Employer-funded Health Reimbursement Account (HRA). HSA compatible Medical Plan, FSA Options.
* Pet Health Insurance (dog & cats).
* Traditional and Roth 40l(k) Plans.
* Generous vacation leave starts with 3 weeks annual accrual. 10 paid holidays. Sick time off.
* Cell phone reimbursement.

*Amprius Technologies is committed to promoting an equal employment opportunity workplace environment and is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expressions, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information (GINA), protected veteran status, or any characteristic protected by law. The Company’s policy is to recruit, hire, train, promote, and administer all employment-related matters based on an individual’s qualifications, abilities, and efforts without regard to protected status.*

jobs.title: Senior Officer, Patient Access
jobs.description:
**Background**

The California Institute for Regenerative Medicine (CIRM) is a state agency created by California voters to accelerate stem cell and gene therapies for people with unmet medical needs. Since 2004, Californians have entrusted CIRM with $8.5 billion to accelerate promising discoveries through clinical trials, train a regenerative medicine workforce, strengthen the state’s biotechnology economy, and expand access to transformative treatments. Today, CIRM is pioneering new models of therapy development and accelerating medical breakthroughs that change lives — in California and around the world. For more information, visit www.cirm.ca.gov.

  

**General Statement**

The Patient Access (PA) Team collaborates across CIRM’s core programs to foster innovative care delivery models and enhance the accessibility of regenerative medicine therapies. The PA Team’s operational goal is to enhance access to clinical trials and approved therapies for all Californians by coordinating clinical infrastructure networks, by supporting market access & patient access strategic planning for CIRM-funded therapies, and by advancing access and affordability research. Additionally, the PA Team serves as a bridge to policymakers and payers, coordinating execution of CIRM’s Access & Affordability strategy as well as coordinating CIRM’s Accessibility and Affordability Working Group (AAWG) as outlined in Proposition 14.

  

The Senior Officer, Patient Access will fill a critical role within the PA team by supporting CIRM-funded preclinical and clinical stage projects on stage-appropriate patient access and market access strategic planning activities. The role will develop and update patient access planning requirements for CIRM preclinical and clinical project funding programs, will be responsible for reviewing the progress of stage-appropriate planning activities, and will identify trends and opportunities for supporting enhanced patient access to CIRM-funded therapies. This role requires independent judgment, cross-functional influence, and deep subject matter expertise in development and execution of patient access and market access strategies for cell and gene therapies.

**Implement Patient Access Planning Requirements**

* Develop, implement, and maintain stage-appropriate patient access and market access planning requirements for CIRM-funded preclinical and clinical programs.
* Serve as a primary point of contact and subject matter resource for CIRM applicants and awardees navigating patient access planning requirements.
* Identify, recruit, and onboard leading experts to serve as reviewers for evaluating patient access planning components of CIRM grant applications and as external advisors for assess patient access planning progress across CIRM awards.

  

**Support Patient Access Planning for CIRM-Funded Therapies**

* Provide guidance to prospective applicants and current awardees on stage-appropriate patient access planning requirements, application expectations, and budget justification for access planning activities.
* Identify and curate resources, consultants, service providers, and best practices to support CIRM awardees in executing patient access and market access planning activities.
* Work closely with the Programs Teams to monitor and track progress of patient access, market access, and commercialization planning activities across CIRM's preclinical and clinical portfolio.
* Review and adjudicate patient access planning milestone reports and support Programs Teams’ approval of operational milestones and associated funding disbursements for preclinical and clinical stage awards.
* Collaborate with the Associate Director of Patient Access to facilitate use of CIRM's clinical infrastructure for enabling patient access to CIRM-funded therapies.
* Participate in Late-Stage Portfolio Management to track and support pre-commercialization and post-approval patient access activities for CIRM-funded therapies.

  

**Conduct Portfolio-Level Analysis & Contribute to CIRM Strategy Execution**

* Collate and analyze trends in patient access, market access, and commercialization strategies across CIRM's active portfolio.
* Track post-approval real world patient access to CIRM-funded therapies and benchmark against industry landscape
* Report portfolio findings and insights to the CIRM Access & Affordability Working Group (AAWG) to inform CIRM's overall Access & Affordability strategy.
* Collaborate with Patient Access Team leadership and the AAWG to identify gaps and additional resources needed to support patient access to CIRM-funded therapies.

* Support the Patient Access Team and AAWG in evaluating and advancing innovative financial and reimbursement models that promote affordability and sustainability of CIRM-funded therapies.

  

**Establish Thought Leadership**

* Routinely engage with payers, providers, patient advocates, health economists and therapy developers to maintain current knowledge and thought leadership on patient access and market access strategies.
* Monitor and analyze trends in payer coverage, reimbursement policy, and healthcare delivery relevant to cell and gene therapies to maintain current awareness and inform CIRM strategy and awardee support.
* Represent CIRM in scientific, industry, regulatory and policy forums.

  

**Required Qualifications (Experience and Education)**

* Bachelor’s degree in public health, Public Policy, Business Administration, Healthcare Management, Health Economics, Life Sciences, or a related field relevant to development and commercial delivery of biologic drug products.
* Minimum 5 years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, with direct involvement in development or executing strategies across pre-commercialization planning, launch planning, market access, patient access, payer strategy, HEOR, government affairs or similar commercial roles.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD

At Sequoia Home Health and Hospice, we’re passionate about our work and take pride in the quality of service we provide. Our community is uniquely diverse, and it’s our aim to fulfill the unique needs of our patients through excellent individualized care.

Our focus is to help facilitate a smooth and safe transition home and provide life-changing service with the amount of care and dignity our patients and their families deserve.

**Sequoia is growing and looking for experienced, compassionate Intake Coordinator to join our team!**

**SUMMARY**

The Intake Coordinator is responsible for managing all aspects of the patient intake process including communicating directly with patients and families, data entry, establishing and maintaining positive relationships with customers and referral sources, responding to customer requests and concerns, facilitating a daily intake stand up meeting, and managing the insurance verification and authorization processes.

**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

* The Intake Coordinator directs all daily patient referral and intake operations including providing direct oversight of the establishment and implementation of intake policies.
* Directs the implementation of improved work methods and procedures to ensure patients are admitted in accordance with policy.
* Establishes and maintains positive working relationships with current and potential referral sources.
* Ensures seamless transition of patients to home care by providing direct oversight of patient education and preparation for home care, plan of care initiation, and coordination of care with multiple service providers.
* Ensures maximum third party reimbursement through direct oversight of insurance verification and authorization processes.
* Maintains comprehensive working knowledge of Home Health contractual relationships and ensures that patients are admitted according to contract provisions.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

* The Intake Coordinator must have healthcare experience, preferably in referrals/intake in a home health environment.
* A nursing background is preferred but not required.
* Demonstrates good communication, negotiation, and public relations skills.
* Demonstrates autonomy, assertiveness, flexibility and cooperation in performing job responsibilities.

**Why Sequoia Home Health?**

Sequoia Home Health **is part of the Cornerstone/Pennant Group** with close to 80 locations throughout the country. **While we are part of a large family, we operate as a local team.** We understand we are nothing without great employees! It is through our team’s dedication to deliver life changing service that we become the “provider of choice” in the community that we serve. **Join a culture of high performers** who are on a mission to create the best Home Health and Hospice agency in the Bay Area!

**What makes us unique** besides our culture of high performers and exceptional care? At Sequoia Home Health, we foster an environment where clinicians and staff members have an unprecedented level of freedom to create and implement the programs that will best serve their patients and communities. We operate with the Core Values of CAPLICO in mind:

* Celebration
* Accountability
* Passion for Learning
* Love One Another
* Intelligent Risk Taking
* Customer Second
* Ownership

We’d love to meet with you if you are passionate about giving exceptional patient care and creating the best Home Health and Hospice agency in the Bay Area!

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Learning & Development - Tech
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission *to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence*. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

**About the Role:**

As Senior Program Manager, Learning & Development - Tech, you will continue to develop and operate a best-in-class global Onboarding & Learning Programs for Crusoe’s global manager population. You will also develop and oversee Crusoe's Team Effectiveness Project. This role is ideal for an experienced L&D strategist who moves quickly, thrives in fast-paced environments, and brings instructional precision, big-picture thinking, and operational excellence.

You will balance high-level strategy with hands-on execution—designing and facilitating manager experiences, curating learning journeys for teams & individuals, and establishing data-driven feedback loops that resonate with our Tech population. Partnering directly with senior leaders across engineering, data center operations, and Employee Success you will ensure our Tech population is equipped to scale with Crusoe’s rapid growth.

**What You'll Be Working On:**

* Onboarding Program: Facilitation and partner with your teammates to keep our Crusoe Onboarding experience …
* Manager Program Facilitation: Facilitate and continuously evolve Crusoe’s Manager Program (“Manager Bootcamp”)
* Tech Onboarding Journey Curation: Build a cohesive, end-to-end development journey that connects our Tech population to Crusoe’s mission, business model, and organizational impact.
* Team Effectiveness: Work with Tech Employee Success Partners to understand what kind of support Tech teams need. Design & facilitate Tech team offsites, deliver Working Genius, DiSC and 5 Dysfunctions of a Team content.
* Modular & Functional Tracks: Partner with internal teams (HR / People, Talent Development, senior leadership) to build modular and team-specific development tracks tailored to technical, and data center operational teams.
* Program Operations & Metrics: Build robust measurement frameworks and feedback loops to evaluate program effectiveness, track leadership performance metrics, and optimize operational delivery.

**What You'll Bring to the Team:**

* 8–10+ Years of L&D Leadership: Proven track record in Learning & Development, Organizational Development, or Instructional Design, with explicit experience scaling manager programs inside technical, engineering organizations.
* Technical Org Fluency: Deep understanding of how engineering and technical operations leads work best, what motivates them, and how to build credibility in highly technical cultures.
* Data-Driven Approach: Expertise using workforce analytics and learning metrics to evaluate program ROI, identify performance risks, and justify strategic interventions.
* Program Execution: Equal parts strategic architect and hands-on builder; comfortable designing frameworks from scratch in ambiguous, fast-growing environments.
* Enthusiasm for Travel: Willingness and ability to travel to global offices, and data centers as needed (approx. 25% travel).

**Bonus Points**

* Organizational Development Background: Advanced grounding in adult learning theory or organizational effectiveness.
* Modern L&D Tech Stack: Hands-on familiarity with tools such as WorkRamp, Lattice, Confluence, or modern LMS/knowledge platforms.
* Infrastructure Tech Context: Genuine curiosity about AI systems, hardware manufacturing, and the physical data center infrastructure powering future technologies.
* Certified Trainer for Working Genius, DiSC, SLII, 5 Dysfunctions of a Team, etc

**Benefits:**

* Competitive compensation and equity packages
* Restricted Stock Units
* Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs
* Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance
* Employer contributions to HSA account
* Paid parental leave
* Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability
* Professional development & tuition reimbursement
* Mental health & wellness support
* Commuter benefits (parking & transit)
* Cell phone stipend
* 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary
* Volunteer time off
* Global travel insurance & emergency assistance
* Daily meals allowance
* Additional perks & programs specific to location

**Compensation Range**

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 - $195,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

This is an exciting fixed-term opportunity for a seasoned L&D Specialist to join the Learning Programs team and support Unity’s cultural transformation. jobs.title: Continuum of Care (CoC) Program Manager - Dept of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (2917 TPV)
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Appointment Type:** This is a Temporary Provisional (TPV) position excluded by the Charter from the competitive Civil Service examination process. It is considered "at will" and shall serve at the discretion of the Department Head. This position will be subject to the Permanent Civil Service examination process at a later date. Successful participation in the Permanent Civil Service examination and selection through an open competitive process is needed in order to be considered for the permanent appointment.

**Application Opening:** October 7, 2026

**Application Deadline:** May close anytime but not before October 22, 2026, at 11:59 PM (PST)

**Compensation Range:** $129,636 - $157,612 annually

**Recruitment ID:** RTF0168077-01142975

**Who We Are**

Through the provision of coordinated, compassionate, and high‐quality services, the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH) strives to make homelessness in San Francisco rare, brief, and one-time. The Department provides assistance and support to homeless and at‐risk youth, adults and families to prevent imminent episodes of homelessness and end homelessness for people in San Francisco. Services including outreach, homelessness prevention, emergency shelter, drop‐in centers, transitional housing, supportive housing, short‐term rental subsidies, and support services to help people exit homelessness. For more information on the department, please visit our https://hsh.sfgov.org/.

**What We Do**

San Francisco is a pioneer in homeless services and a leader in providing supportive housing as a permanent exit from homelessness. The Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH), founded in 2016, is a national leader in the movement to end homelessness by developing a coordinated, equity-driven, client-focused system of compassionate services while piloting innovative models, and implementing best practice solutions with measurable results.

HSH’s Homelessness Response System (HRS) funds, oversees and implements a system of care that shelters, houses, and serves approximately 15,000 people daily. Major programs include: street outreach and service connection through the Homeless Outreach Team (SFHOT); 3,600 +bed shelter system for transitional age youth, adults and families including shelters for members of the LGBTQ community; rapid rehousing rental subsidies for families, adults, older adults, and transitional aged youth; the Problem Solving and flexible financial assistance programs; and robust supportive housing programs with over 14,500 units which provide housing and services to formerly homeless transitional age youth, individuals, and families.

 **Job Description**

The Continuum of Care (CoC) Program Manager is responsible for overseeing and managing the CoC Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH) projects that receive rental assistance, supportive services, operating, and administrative budget line items. On an annual basis, the San Francisco Continuum of Care receives over $48 million in funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to administer CoC programs administered by the San Francisco Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing.

The CoC Program Manager supervises staff who work on compliance related to verification of CoC PSH program eligibility, income certifications and recertifications, and the coordination of Housing Quality Standards (HQS) inspections. The position reports to the CoC Program Supervisor and is a member of the Continuum of Care team at HSH.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Supervises and manages the performance of staff
* Under general direction, oversees a portfolio of CoC-program related units and/or services, regularly communicating with stakeholders to provide technical support related to CoC program compliance, contracting, and invoicing.
* Reviews and approves forms and documents related to CoC subsidy billing, such as CoC Rental Assistance Invoice review, Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) Contracts, HAP Contract Amendments, Vacancy Loss Claims, and Property Damage Claims, and security deposits.
* Regularly provides input on program and policy development of CoC team, including the CoC Operations manual, the CoC Subsidy Termination Policy, and the CoC and ESG Desk Guide.
* Proposes and provides solutions to problems that arise within the portfolio, including developing and implementing systems and best practices to support achievement of departmental and grant goals.
* Program manages grant agreements – develops the scope of services and budget for agreements; reviews budget revisions; reviews and submits budget modification requests; and participates in program monitoring.
* Performs analyses on grant utilization and spend down, including other statistical analyses and reports to inform policy and funding decisions to improve on‐going operations of CoC PSH programs and other activities related to the CoC PSH portfolio.
* Reviews invoices and reports in the Contracts Administration, Reporting, and Billing Online (CARBON) system and update CARBON.
* Actively participates in the development, implementation and ongoing operations of the Coordinated Entry (CE) process and the Online Navigation and Entry (ONE) system.

**Company Description**

**Appointment Type:** This is a Temporary Provisional (TPV) position excluded by the Charter from the competitive Civil Service examination process. It is considered "at will" and shall serve at the discretion of the Department Head. This position will be subject to the Permanent Civil Service examination process at a later date. Successful participation in the Permanent Civil Service examination and selection through an open competitive process is needed in order to be considered for the permanent appointment.

Application Opening: October 7, 2026

Application Deadline: May close anytime but not before October 22, 2026, at 11:59 PM (PST)

Compensation Range: $129,636 - $157,612 annually

Recruitment ID: RTF0168079-01156693

**Who We Are**

Through the provision of coordinated, compassionate, and high‐quality services, the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH) strives to make homelessness in San Francisco rare, brief, and one time. The Department provides assistance and support to homeless and at‐risk youth, adults, and families to prevent imminent episodes of homelessness and end homelessness for people in San Francisco. Services including outreach, homelessness prevention, emergency shelter, drop‐in centers, transitional housing, supportive housing, short‐term rental subsidies, and support services to help people exit homelessness. For more information about the department, please visit our website at https://hsh.sfgov.org.

**What We Do**

San Francisco is a pioneer in homeless services and a leader in providing supportive housing as a permanent exit from homelessness. The Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing (HSH), founded in 2016, is a national leader in the movement to end homelessness by developing a coordinated, equity-driven, client-focused system of compassionate services while piloting innovative models, and implementing best practice solutions with measurable results.

HSH’s Homelessness Response System (HRS) funds, oversees and implements a system of care that shelters, houses, and serves approximately 15,000 people daily. Major programs include: street outreach and service connection through the Homeless Outreach Team (SFHOT); 3,600+ bed shelter system for transitional age youth, adults and families including shelters for members of the LGBTQ community; Rapid Rehousing rental subsidies for families, adults, older adults, and transitional aged youth; the Problem Solving and flexible financial assistance programs; and robust supportive housing programs with over 14,500 units which provide housing and services to formerly homeless transitional age youth, individuals, and families.

 **Job Description**

**What You’ll Be Doing**

The Rapid Rehousing Program Manager supports the planning, implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of Rapid Rehousing programs funded by HSH. Rapid Rehousing provides time-limited rental assistance and supportive services to help people experiencing homelessness obtain housing in the private rental market and transition toward long-term housing stability, including nonprofit provider agreements, program budgets, utilization, housing placements, participant outcomes, and program performance.

HSH has a longstanding portfolio of Rapid Rehousing programs, and the City continues to invest in and expand these programs as part of its Breaking the Cycle strategy. The Program Manager will play a central role in implementing this investment and the next phase of HSH's RRH portfolio, including implementation of newly procured programs and provider agreements, provider and program transitions, and efforts to strengthen and standardize program operations. The position will help ensure that new and existing investments translate into timely referrals and housing placements, strong program utilization, effective provider performance, and successful participant outcomes.

The Program Manager works across HSH and with nonprofit providers, Coordinated Entry, housing partners, other City departments, and governmental and community partners to translate HSH's housing strategies into effective program operations. The position uses program, fiscal, and performance data to identify challenges, develop solutions, and recommend changes to program design, policy, funding, and operations. The Rapid Rehousing Program Manager reports to the Scattered Site Housing Programs Supervisor and is part of HSH's Housing Division.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Manages assigned Rapid Rehousing (RRH) programs and provider grant agreements.
* Implements new and reprocured RRH programs, provider transitions, and other program changes.
* Develops and manages scopes of work, program deliverables, outcome objectives, and grant modifications.
* Monitors program budgets and expenditures and supports budget development, projections, revisions, and modifications.
* Monitors referrals, enrollment, utilization, housing placements, exits, and housing retention outcomes.
* Works with providers to identify and address program performance concerns and improve outcomes.
* Ensures providers deliver housing stabilization and retention services to support participants following housing placement and through successful program exit.
* Analyzes program, fiscal, and ONE System/HMIS data to identify trends, barriers, and opportunities for program improvement.
* Monitors provider data quality and works with providers and HSH staff to resolve reporting issues.
* Develops and updates RRH policies, procedures, program standards, and operational guidance in coordination with HSH leadership.
* Conducts annual program monitoring and follows up on findings and corrective actions.
* Coordinates with Coordinated Entry and providers to support timely referrals and maximize program utilization.

jobs.title: UAS Operations Specialist - Ground Support
jobs.description:
**About the Role**
------------------

As a **UAS Operations Ground Support Specialist**, you'll join Flight Operations in a **qualified Commercial Ground Support position** supporting safe, **compliant UAS delivery operations under Part 135**. All hires complete **required training and qualification under the company's FAA-approved training program** before independently performing assigned duties.

You'll work alongside Remote Pilots in Command (RPICs), Flight Operations leadership, and Maintenance to **support aircraft readiness, safe ground operations, and mission execution** through disciplined procedures and clear communication.

You'll also work cross-functionally with Flight Test, Engineering, and other teams to **support Part 107 testing**, developmental operations, and system validation within applicable authorizations and established safety controls.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Serve as **qualified Commercial Ground Support** within Flight Operations **for Part 135 UAS operations** once trained, qualified, and authorized.
* **Complete training delivered by a qualified Ground Instructor under the company's FAA-approved training program** and required competency evaluations. Initial-cadre members complete the applicable **FAA qualification and evaluation process.**
* Maintain **required qualifications, recurrent training,** proficiency, and standardization requirements.
* **Support aircraft preparation**, staging, payload handling, battery management, equipment setup, launch and recovery, and aircraft turnaround **within assigned responsibilities.**
* **Verify** aircraft, payload, equipment, and **operating-area readiness in accordance with assigned Ground Support procedures and checklists.**
* **Apply applicable Part 135 requirements, company manuals, SOPs, checklists, Operations Specifications, exemptions, waivers, and operating limitations** relevant to assigned duties.
* **Coordinate with the RPIC** and operational personnel throughout missions, **maintaining situational awareness and timely communication** of ground conditions and aircraft readiness.
* **Pause unsafe ground activities and promptly escalate concerns through established channels**. Flight command authority remains with the RPIC.
* **Identify and report hazards**, **aircraft discrepancies, equipment damage, and procedural deviations** through established safety and maintenance channels.
* Maintain accurate training, qualification, operational, and equipment **records required for assigned activities.**
* **Support abnormal and emergency operations within defined Ground Support responsibilities,** including required drills and emergency procedure training.
* **Work cross-functionally with Flight Test, Engineering, and other teams to support Part 107 testing**, developmental operations, demonstrations, and validation within assigned duties and applicable authorizations.
* **Provide structured operational feedback** and contribute to improvements in ground procedures, SOPs, checklists, equipment, and training materials.
* When qualified and designated, qualify additional Ground Support crew members under the **FAA-approved training program**. **Training duties require separate qualification and designation as a Ground Instructor**.
* **Work outdoors with extended standing**, equipment handling, and **varying weather conditions while following company safety practices and operating limits**.
* **Maintain schedule flexibility** for commercial operations, training, and testing, **including day, evening, and weekend assignments as required**.
* **Participate in the company's FAA/DOT drug and alcohol testing program** when assigned duties are covered under 14 CFR Part 120, **including pre-employment drug testing and applicable ongoing testing under 49 CFR Part 40**.

**You're Excited About This Opportunity Because You Will…**
-----------------------------------------------------------

* **Hold a qualified operational position** supporting commercial Part 135 UAS delivery.
* **Develop through an FAA-approved training program** with defined qualification and proficiency standards.
* **Work alongside pilots and Maintenance** to support aircraft readiness and safe mission execution.
* **Collaborate with technical teams during Part 107 flight testing** and system validation.
* **Be considered for additional qualification responsibilities** as your proficiency and program needs develop.
* Contribute directly to safe, standardized, and scalable drone delivery operations.

**We're Excited About You Because…**
------------------------------------

* **You Have Relevant Operational Experience:**  
  Experience in UAS, aviation ground operations, logistics, maintenance, or another safety-critical environment is preferred.
* **You Meet and Maintain Qualification Standards:**  
  You hold a valid Part 107 certificate and you can complete required training, competency evaluations, recurrent training, and standardization requirements and maintain eligibility for assigned duties.
* **You're Safety-Minded and Procedurally Disciplined:**  
  You consistently follow manuals, SOPs, checklists, and operating limitations, recognize hazards, and pause or escalate activities when conditions are unsafe.
* **You're Hands-On and Detail-Oriented:**  
  You're comfortable handling aircraft, batteries, payloads, and support equipment, and can identify incorrect configurations, discrepancies, and abnormal conditions.
* **You Communicate and Collaborate Clearly:**  
  You provide timely, accurate operational callouts and work effectively with pilots, Maintenance, Flight Test, and cross-functional teams within defined responsibilities.
* **You Document with Discipline:**  
  You maintain accurate training, qualification, operational, and equipment records and report observations clearly to support traceability, compliance, and continuous improvement.
* **You're Prepared for Additional Responsibility:**  
  Additional qualification or G

jobs.title: Insurance Claims Operations Associate
jobs.description:
**About the Team**
------------------

DoorDash's Risk & Insurance team protects and strengthens our business by developing innovative insurance programs and operational strategies that support millions of deliveries worldwide. We partner across Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Data Science, and Operations to manage risk, improve customer outcomes, and enable the continued growth of one of the world's largest local commerce platforms.

As DoorDash continues to scale globally, Insurance Claims Operations is evolving through artificial intelligence, automation, and digital transformation. Our organization is reimagining how claims are managed by leveraging technology to automate routine work, enhance operational decision-making, and create scalable solutions that improve efficiency while maintaining exceptional customer experiences.

**About the Role**
------------------

DoorDash is seeking an Insurance Claims Operations Associate to join our Claims Operations team. In this role, you will manage the intake, documentation, and follow-up work that keeps cases moving efficiently from first report through resolution.

You will work closely with internal systems, AI-assisted tools, and cross-functional partners to ensure every case is accurately created, updated, and progressed. Your work directly supports the team's ability to deliver timely, high-quality outcomes for the people we serve.

This role is well suited to someone who is detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable managing a high volume of work in a fast-paced environment.

This position will report to a Supervisor, Insurance Claims Operations and is fully remote. Onboarding will take place over the first 4–6 weeks, Monday through Friday. After onboarding, schedules may be assigned on any day Monday through Sunday based on business needs.

**You're excited about this opportunity because you will**
----------------------------------------------------------

* Execute high-volume intake and case processing across multiple channels
* Prepare and submit FNOL details for claim establishment
* Review, organize, and accurately input incoming documentation and attachments
* Identify and resolve missing, inconsistent, or incomplete information using defined workflows and tools
* Support operational workflows by addressing routing issues, intake gaps, and system exceptions
* Maintain accurate, consistent, and up-to-date data across multiple systems
* Manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, production-driven environment while meeting daily performance targets
* Communicate effectively with internal teams to ensure timely and efficient case progression
* Contribute to continuous process improvements as workflows evolve with automation and AI

**We're excited about you because…**
------------------------------------

* 1+ years of experience in operations, claims intake, insurance support, or a similar high-volume environment
* Strong attention to detail and ability to follow structured processes consistently
* Comfortable working across multiple systems and tools simultaneously
* Ability to manage time effectively and meet daily productivity expectations
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion
* Experience in insurance, claims, or risk operations is a plus (but not required)
* A process-driven mindset with a focus on accuracy and efficiency
* Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment
* Strong organizational skills and ability to manage repetitive workflows with consistency
* Adaptability as tools, systems, and workflows evolve with automation

Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis

**About DoorDash**
------------------

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.  
  
DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees' happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

**Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion**
---------------------------------------------

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. jobs.title: Senior Regulatory Quality Program Manager
jobs.description:
Join the transformative team at City of Hope, where we're changing lives and making a real difference in the fight against cancer, diabetes, and other life-threatening illnesses. City of Hope’s growing national system includes its Los Angeles campus, a network of clinical care locations across Southern California, a new cancer center in Orange County, California, and treatment facilities in Atlanta, Chicago and Phoenix. our dedicated and compassionate employees are driven by a common mission: To deliver the cures of tomorrow to the people who need them today.

**\*\* This is a Fully Remote Opportunity within the United States\*\***

**Position Summary:**

The Senior Regulatory Quality Program Manager is responsible for ensuring the organization complies with regulatory requirements through quality performance measurement, data integrity, and EHR-enabled reporting programs. This position will support enterprise regulatory quality programs, including development and implementation of EHR-aligned workflows, data capture processes, and performance measurement frameworks. Responsible for staying up to date with federal and state regulatory requirements and translating requirements into quality measure specifications, reporting logic, and data capture workflows within the EHR and analytics platforms. This position provides the connection between healthcare clinical federal and state regulatory programs, EHR systems, data structures, and regulatory quality performance outcomes.

The Senior Regulatory Quality Program Manager is responsible for leading and coordinating enterprise-level programs that support regulatory compliance, quality performance reporting, regulatory measurement, and EHR-enabled compliance programs across City of Hope. This role operates in close partnership with executive leadership to support enterprise-wide regulatory strategy, program execution, and performance oversight.

**As a successful candidate, you will:**

**Regulatory Quality Metrics, Data, and Program Execution:**

Serves as a subject matter expert in healthcare regulatory programs, including CMS quality reporting and interoperability requirements, with a primary focus on quality performance measurement and data integrity. Monitors evolving federal and state regulatory requirements and translates these into regulatory measure specifications, reporting logic, and EHR-aligned data capture workflows.

Coordinates the planning, implementation, and execution of regulatory programs (e.g., MIPS, eCQMs, registry-based submissions), ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant reporting. Evaluates the operational and financial impact of regulatory performance and supports optimization of data capture, documentation, and reporting processes.

Partners with Quality Analytics, Clinical Operations, and Information Technology teams to align EHR workflows, data structures, and report outputs with regulatory requirements. Provides guidance and education to stakeholders on measure definitions, documentation standards, and regulatory program expectations. Ensures measurable outcomes through consistent tracking of performance metrics, reporting deliverables, and program milestones.

**Quality Performance Measurement, Validation, and Improvement:**

* Leads ongoing evaluation of regulatory quality measure performance, including data completeness, accuracy, and alignment between clinical workflows and reporting requirements. Validates measure logic, including numerator/denominator integrity, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and data mapping across EHR and reporting systems.
* Analyzes complex performance data to identify gaps, variation, and opportunities for improvement, and recommends EHR build changes, workflow modifications, and documentation enhancements to improve measure performance and reporting accuracy.
* Coordinates data collection and abstraction activities across assigned resources to support regulatory submissions, including prioritization of work, issue resolution, and alignment to measure specifications and timelines. Collaborates with clinical, operational, and analytics stakeholders to resolve discrepancies and ensure consistency in reported data.
* Develops and maintains documentation of regulatory measure logic, data definitions, workflows, and reporting processes to support validation, auditability, and sustainable program execution. Supports clinical leadership in operationalizing regulatory quality programs and performance improvement initiatives aligned with organizational goals.
* Follows established City of Hope and department policies, procedures, objectives, performance improvement, attendance, safety, environmental, and infection control guidelines, including adherence to the workplace code of Conduct and Compliance Plan.
* Practices a high level of integrity and honesty in maintaining confidentiality.
* Performs other related duties as assigned or requested.

**Your qualifications should include:**

**Minimum Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare, information systems, business or related field

**Minimum Experience:**

* Seven years of relevant experience in healthcare regulatory programs, quality analytics, clinical informatics, or program management within a healthcare environment
* Demonstrated experience working with regulatory quality reporting, EHR-based data capture, and cross-functional program coordination required

**City of Hope employees pay is based on the following criteria: work experience, qualifications, and work location.**

**City of Hope is an equal opportunity employer.**

At Bitfocus, our mission is simple but ambitious: help end homelessness. We do that by building and supporting Clarity Human Services, the technology that powers communities across the country in their work to connect people experiencing homelessness with the resources they need.

We're a team that leads with care, innovates with insider knowledge, and believes deeply in the power of community. We take pride in what we build, support one another through hard problems, and embrace smart risks in service of meaningful impact.

jobs.title: Billing Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Billing Operations Manager  
  
GridSource is seeking a Billing Operations Manager to lead the billing analyst team within our Managed Services Division. This role owns the accuracy and timeliness of billing across multiple markets and service lines — FTTx fiber installation, Multi-Dwelling Unit (MDU), and Buried Service Wire (BSW) work — and is responsible for the people, processes, and controls that turn completed field work into correct, on-time invoices. You will lead a team of analysts, coordinate the inputs that drive each billing cycle, and build the process improvements that keep billing clean as the business grows.  
  
What You'll Do  
The Billing Operations Manager sits at the center of how GridSource gets paid. You will manage and develop a team of billing analysts, hold the line on billing accuracy, and keep multiple concurrent work streams moving so that every market bills on time. Just as important, you will improve how the work gets done — strengthening controls, closing gaps, and building repeatable processes — and report clearly and concisely to the EVP and senior leadership on billing status, risks, and results. Success means invoices that are correct the first time, billing cycles that close on schedule, and a team that gets steadily better at both.  

*Team Leadership & Development*

* Lead, develop, and manage the performance of a team of billing analysts working across markets.
* Set clear standards for accuracy, turnaround, and follow-through, and hold the team to them.
* Balance and assign workload so billing deadlines are met without single points of failure.

*Billing Accuracy & Controls*

* Own the accuracy, completeness, and auditability of invoices across FTTx, MDU, and BSW work in multiple markets.
* Reconcile completed field work to billed amounts, and identify and resolve discrepancies before invoices go out.
* Establish and maintain the controls that prevent revenue leakage, missed billing, and avoidable customer disputes.

*Multi-Workstream Coordination & On-Time Delivery*

* Coordinate the inputs that drive each billing cycle — field production data, project records, and rate/contract terms — across teams and markets.
* Keep concurrent billing work streams on schedule so each market closes on time.
* Flag and clear the bottlenecks that threaten a billing deadline.

*Process Improvement & Systems*

* Analyze the current billing process end to end and build improvements that raise both accuracy and speed.
* Design repeatable, documented workflows and controls that scale as markets and volume grow.
* Partner with operations, finance, and systems teams to improve the tools and data behind billing.

*Reporting & Executive Communication*

* Provide succinct, numbers-first reporting on billing status, risks, and results to the EVP and C-suite.
* Surface issues early with a recommended course of action, not just a problem.
* Translate billing detail into the few metrics leadership needs to make decisions.

What You'll Need  

*Core Competencies (Required)*

* Team leadership — a proven ability to lead, develop, and get results from a team.
* Billing accuracy & controls — a track record of owning correct, auditable, on-time billing and the controls behind it.
* Multi-workstream coordination — able to keep several concurrent billing streams and deadlines on track across markets.
* Process improvement & systems thinking — sees how the whole process fits together and builds durable improvements, with a continuous-improvement mindset.
* Executive communication — succinct, numbers-first communication to EVP and C-suite audiences.

*Experience & Logistics*

* Prior experience leading or supervising a team (required).
* Working knowledge of billing for FTTx fiber installation, MDU, and BSW work in a multi-market environment.
* Comfort working across billing/ERP systems and spreadsheets, with strong attention to detail.
* Remote role; must be available during core business hours of 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Central Time.
* Less than 10% travel.

*Preferred Qualifications*

* Experience in telecommunications, broadband, or construction / field-services billing.
* Experience building or overhauling a billing process, not just running one.
* Familiarity with job-costing, rate/contract structures, and production-based billing.
* Experience billing for major carriers or MSOs.
* Familiarity with billing-system implementations or reporting / BI tools.

*Work Environment*

* Fully remote, with required availability during 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Central Time.
* Less than 10% travel.
* Close coordination with the EVP, operations and project teams, and finance across multiple markets.

What We Offer

* Health, vision, and dental insurance
* Paid time off (PTO)
* 401(k) retirement plan
* Paid sick leave in accordance with applicable state and local laws

Why Work For GridSource?  
GridSource is a full-service utility contractor specializing in telecommunications and broadband construction, as well as underground construction for the natural gas distribution industry.  
We believe our employees are our greatest asset. When you join GridSource, you become part of a team that values your success and supports your professional development. Our leadership team is committed to mentoring employees, providing training, and creating opportunities to grow within the company.  
GridSource is proud to support U.S. military members, veterans, and their families. Active-duty military members, transitioning service members, and veterans are encouraged to apply.  
GridSource is committed to equal employment opportunity and to recruiting, hiring, and promoting qualified individuals without regard to race, color, gender, religion, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, or other protected status. GridSource is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer and will provide reasonable accommodations in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities.

jobs.title: Utility Operations Manager
jobs.description:
**About QE Solar**

QE Solar is one of the nation's largest independent solar and BESS operations and maintenance providers, with over 15 years of operating experience. We manage 10 GW of solar and 7.5 GWh of BESS across 44 states, supporting asset owners with multi-hundred MW utility solar projects and large standalone BESS systems. We're pure-play O&M. That focus means our entire organization is built around one thing: keeping solar and storage assets running well. Our technicians carry broad OEM certifications, and our in-house capabilities span MV/HV electrical, vegetation management, engineering, and capital improvements, to streamline asset management for project owners.

QE Solar is seeking a highly motivated **Utility Field Operations Manager** to lead field operations supporting utility-scale solar and battery storage assets throughout North America. This role is responsible for overseeing field personnel, contractor coordination, operational performance, safety compliance, maintenance execution, and customer satisfaction across a portfolio of renewable energy assets.

The ideal candidate is a strong operational leader with utility-scale solar experience, excellent communication skills, and the ability to drive accountability, safety, and execution across geographically dispersed teams.

**Travel: 25–35%**

**Key Responsibilities**

**Field Operations Leadership**

Oversee operations and maintenance activities across assigned utility-scale solar, BESS, substation, and MV/HV assets.

Lead Plant Managers responsible for utility sites and ensure consistent execution of site operations, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, outage support, inspections, and compliance requirements.

Ensure Plant Managers maintain strong site ownership, including daily site walks, SCADA review, work planning, work order review, safety meetings, contractor coordination, and customer-ready documentation.

Support safe execution of utility-site work involving inverters, trackers, transformers, switchgear, substations, BESS, collection systems, and balance-of-plant equipment.

Drive accountability for LOTO, NFPA 70E, switching procedures, energized work controls, site-specific procedures, and customer/regulatory requirements.

Monitor and support work order progression, PM/CM completion, FWC-to-Complete closeout, backlog reduction, and documentation quality across assigned sites.

Provide coaching, mentorship, performance management, and leadership development for Plant Managers and site-level personnel.

Coordinate with internal engineering, ROC/control center, asset management, safety, compliance, and subcontractors to resolve site issues and maintain asset performance.

Support workforce planning, outage coverage, contractor mobilization, staffing needs, scheduling, and resource allocation across assigned utility sites.

**Maintenance & Asset Performance**

* Oversee preventive, corrective, and emergency maintenance execution across assigned utility-scale solar, BESS, substation, MV/HV, and balance-of-plant assets.
* Ensure Plant Managers are effectively planning, prioritizing, and driving completion of PMs, CMs, inspections, outage work, and site corrective actions.
* Monitor site operational performance, equipment health, availability, downtime drivers, and recurring failures to ensure uptime and performance targets are achieved.
* Partner with engineering, ROC/control center, SCADA support, OEMs, and technical teams to resolve complex inverter, tracker, transformer, switchgear, SCADA, BESS, medium-voltage, and balance-of-system issues.
* Support escalation and resolution of utility-site issues involving outages, switching coordination, equipment failures, alarms, contractor support, and customer-impacting events.
* Drive operational excellence initiatives focused on reliability, work order discipline, PM/CM compliance, documentation quality, efficiency, and cost control.
* Ensure Plant Managers complete accurate maintenance documentation, work orders, photos, inspection results, test records, and reporting in a timely and customer-ready manner.
* Monitor FWC status, overdue work orders, aging backlog, and documentation gaps to ensure completed field work is reviewed, closed, and reported properly.

**Safety & Compliance**

* Champion QE Solar’s safety culture across assigned utility-scale solar, BESS, substation, and MV/HV sites.
* Ensure Plant Managers are consistently reinforcing site safety expectations, toolbox talks, hazard identification, pre-job planning, LOTO, JHAs, and safe work execution.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, NFPA 70E, company safety procedures, LOTO requirements, switching procedures, energized work controls, and customer site-specific policies.
* Support safe execution of utility-site work involving inverters, trackers, transformers, switchgear, substations, collection systems, BESS, and balance-of-plant equipment.
* Conduct field audits, site safety observations, Plant Manager check-ins, incident reviews, and corrective action follow-up across assigned sites.
* Verify safety documentation, permits, switching orders, LOTO records, inspection findings, and corrective actions are completed accurately and on time.
* Ensure subcontractors follow QE Solar safety expectations, customer requirements, site access rules, work procedures, and documentation standards.
* Escalate safety, compliance, or regulatory concerns immediately when issues create risk to personnel, equipment, customer commitments, or site reliability.

**Customer & Stakeholder Management**
